content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge is resolving a collision between the challenger's Link 6 and the defender's own chain (Isaiah 7:14 read with 8:3, 8:8 and 9:6-7), which is the situation the rule governs.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"the sign itself does not state the mechanism","rule_words":"the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"'weighs chain against chain by footing': the judge's text could be read as a bare summary of both sides' moves, or as a ruling resting on a verse-level test. Because the ruling ends on a single verse's silence rather than on any comparison of footing, I took the second reading.","why":"The judge calls the matter underdetermined because the sign verse does not state the mechanism, which is the stating-verse test the rule retires, and never weighs the defender's chain against the challenger's by footing."}
